chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ja'far ibn Isa, who said:

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! A woman dies, and her father claims that he had lent her some of the possessions and servants that were with her. Is his claim accepted without proof, or is his claim not accepted except with proof?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote to him: 'It is permissible without proof.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'And I wrote to him that if the husband of the deceased woman, or her father-in-law, or her mother-in-law, were to claim regarding her possessions or her servants, similar to what her father had claimed regarding the loan of some of the possessions or the servants, would they be in the same status as the father in the claim?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'No.'
ai.seo_question: Can a father claim lent items from his deceased daughter's estate without proof?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of 'bi-la bayyinah' (acceptance without proof) in inheritance disputes, specifically granting the deceased woman's father a privileged status to claim lent items or servants from her estate without requiring evidence. In contrast, the husband or his parents are not accorded this same presumption, highlighting a nuanced distinction in Shia jurisprudence regarding familial hierarchy and evidentiary burdens in estate settlement.
